clue.text: About to stop bandits with a naughty retailers' trick

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece goes into the gap in the other
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of these words are jumbled out of order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A gang of bandits up to a naughty trick that shopkeepers might pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles BANDITS WITH A, and 'to stop' plugs C (circa) into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A con where a cheap advertised item lures shoppers who are then pushed toward a dearer one is a familiar shopkeeping scam.

clue.text: Time to go in a smarter direction — they'd like to have lunch with workers

definitions.text: they'd like to have lunch with workers
definitions.note: workers here are worker ants, which these animals eat

indicators.note: to go in means to be inserted, so the time letter enters the next word

parts.note: neater means tidier, smarter in appearance
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A firm smartening up its direction, its staff lunching with the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees but means worker ants; 'to go in' puts T into A NEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-snouted mammals feed on ants and termites, so worker ants would be their meal.

clue.text: Nameless brown weed in US lake

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

explanation.surface: An unidentified brown weed found growing in an American lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' removes N (name) from TAN, leaving TA; 'weed' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This large freshwater lake on the California-Nevada border is a well-known American lake.

clue.text: Perhaps exposed campers to insult, surrounded by fanatics

indicators.note: surrounded by means the insult word is placed inside the fanatics word

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts, as in health nuts
to dis is slang for to insult

explanation.surface: Campers exposed to abuse from a crowd of fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' suggests out in the open; here it means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: People at a naturist camp go without clothes, so they are exposed campers; 'Perhaps' marks them as one example.

clue.text: Like Britain in decline — capital's revolting

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed capital goes into the decline word

parts.note: to set is to go down, as the sun does

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the capital is written backwards

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of Britain in decline with its capital in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like rebellion in the capital, but it signals writing Latvia's capital backwards; 'Like Britain' points to an island surrounded by water.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation is ringed by the ocean, and the poetic adjective describes exactly that.

clue.text: That one may work or not — dire!

definitions.note: a phrase of purpose, meaning so that one can

indicators.note: to work is to knead or shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a plan: it may or may not work, and it looks dire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a purpose: you do something so that you can achieve another thing.

clue.text: Film wildlife — only the second omnivore

parts.note: a film is a thin covering layer, like a coat

indicators.note: only the second letter of the word wildlife is used

explanation.surface: A wildlife documentary featuring only one omnivore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but it means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: This raccoon relative of the Americas eats fruit, insects and small animals, so it eats both plants and meat.

clue.text: Easily beguile Donald with this?

indicators.note: easily is a loose signal here, the letters falling with ease into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a certain Donald could be fooled with ease by this trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easily' is a stretched anagram signal; the solver may pick whichever Donald suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful, two-faced conduct is just what one would use to trick someone, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: God to blame ultimately in drama (foul one)? No, it was this bloke

definitions.note: the footballer who said a famous 1986 handball goal was scored by the hand of God

indicators.note: foul means corrupt or bad, so these letters are messed up
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letters of to and blame are used

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A footballing row: was God to blame for that foul? No, it was this player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' rearranges GOD + O + E (the last letters of TO and BLAME) + IN DRAMA + A. In the 1986 World Cup, the Argentine said his handball goal was the 'hand of God'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine star blamed God's hand for his handball goal against England, so the real culprit was the player himself.

clue.text: Cast do care — that largely figures

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so these letters are thrown into a new order
largely means most of it, so the word that loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to cast something, with a remark that this mostly adds up to figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts THAT to THA, and 'Cast' mixes it with DO CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solids with eight flat faces are geometric shapes, and figures is the general word for such shapes.

clue.text: 20 across content to look a pillock

definitions.note: the solution to 20 across, an animal that feeds by nibbling leaves and shoots

indicators.note: content as a noun means what something holds, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone happy to look a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads like an adjective (happy) but means the contents of LOOK A PILLOCK. 20 across is BROWSER: an animal that feeds on leaves rather than grass.
explanation.definitionFit: This forest giraffe-relative feeds on leaves from trees, which makes it a classic leaf-eating animal of the type zoologists call browsers.

clue.text: Defy British party

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A call to stand against the British party in power.
explanation.definitionFit: To face up to danger or opposition without flinching is to defy it.

clue.text: Fraud succeeded, turning over liberal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the turning word goes over and around the other letter

parts.note: winding means twisting or turning

explanation.surface: A fraudster gets away with it by switching to the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts WINDING round L, giving WINDLING after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating people out of money by deceit is fraud, so the two nouns name the same crime.

clue.text: Expenses claims politician tried at first to make excuses

indicators.note: claims here means takes in, so the expenses word holds the other letters

parts.note: exes is informal shorthand for expenses
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word tried is used

explanation.surface: An MP's expense claims prompt a string of excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' looks like part of 'expenses claims' but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to release them from it, which is what granting an exemption does.

clue.text: Spin doctor, you might say, is poisonous

definitions.text: Spin doctor, you might say, is poisonous

parts.words: Spin doctor, you might say, is poisonous
parts.note: a spin doctor adds puff, or hype, so could jokingly be called one who adds puff; that phrase is also a venomous African snake

explanation.surface: A jibe that political spin doctors are toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: Puff is hype or exaggerated praise; one who adds it is a 'puff adder', which is really a venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke name for a hype merchant is also the name of a highly venomous African viper.

clue.text: Element of fear oddly gone but I'm unhappy boxing

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the jumble holds the other letters
unhappy means upset, so these letters are rearranged
with the odd letters gone, only the second and fourth letters of fear remain

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off fear but miserable about taking up boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly gone' leaves ER from FEAR; 'unhappy' turns BUT I'M into TBIUM, and 'boxing' puts ER inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare-earth metal, number 65 in the periodic table, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Current issue involves money — first clue one probably won't enjoy retirement

parts.note: in means current or fashionable

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the issue word holds the money letter

parts.note: a son is one's issue, or offspring
the first clue is 1 across, written as I AC with I as one

explanation.surface: A current issue about money, and someone who won't enjoy their pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who struggles to sleep will not enjoy going to bed at night, which is the retirement meant here.

clue.text: Roughly spoken bloke's eaten enough to be comfortable

indicators.note: spoken roughly means said in a broad accent that drops the H, as a Cockney might

parts.note: a bloke who has eaten enough is full, so he's full

explanation.surface: A man who has eaten his fill feels comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H, as in some broad English accents, and 'he's full' becomes ''e's full'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of ease is restful and soothing, a rather literary way of saying comfortable.

clue.text: Novice priest breaks down and loses restraint

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

indicators.note: breaks down means falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novice priest breaks down and stops holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: To act or speak without holding back is to let yourself go, an idiom for dropping self-control.

clue.text: Safari for one brother involves disagreements with sweetheart

indicators.note: involves means includes, so the brother letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: rows are arguments, pronounced to rhyme with cows
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet is E

explanation.surface: A brother caught up in quarrels with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safari' suggests a trip to Africa, but it is Apple's web software.
explanation.definitionFit: Safari is Apple's program for viewing web pages, one example of that kind of internet software.

clue.text: Chance to get hold of Irish teaching assistant — it goes to father's head

definitions.note: father here is a Catholic priest; the clue describes what sits on his head

indicators.note: to get hold of means to grab and hold, so the chance word wraps round the Irish letters

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble

explanation.surface: An opportunity to hire an Irish classroom assistant, and something that goes to Dad's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' suggests a dad but means a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap with ridges worn by Catholic clergy is headwear for a priest addressed as Father.

clue.text: Guard resembled Luxembourg's new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: to take after a parent is to resemble them
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A bodyguard who looked like Luxembourg's newly installed leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new leader' swaps the T at the front of TOOK AFTER for L.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard someone is to protect them and take care of them.

clue.text: Drive round? We won't be moving at this rate

parts.note: O is round in shape

parts.words: We won't be moving at this rate
parts.note: zero miles per hour, written 0 MPH, is the speed of standing still

explanation.surface: Someone asking about a drive around, complaining it is going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests a car trip; it means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of energy and get-up-and-go is vigour, which is what this informal word means.

clue.text: It's stupid — both rejected retiring

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so both words are written backwards

parts.note: dim means slow-witted
it is taken as written, the apostrophe-s being a link

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idea as stupid and rejects both options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both rejected' reverses DIM and IT, giving MID and TI, in the order TI + MID.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy and keeps out of the way, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Article ignoring centrist's clear belief

indicators.note: ignoring the centre means the middle letter of the article word is dropped

parts.note: the is the definite article
net means clear after deductions, as in net profit

explanation.surface: A newspaper article that ignores a centrist's plain belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrist's' looks political but marks the centre letter H of THE for removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle a person or group holds firmly is one of their beliefs.

clue.text: Agree without speaking about old woman — she won't settle

definitions.note: a wanderer of either sex; the clue uses she to fit the old woman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the agreement word wraps round the other

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement silently
ma is slang for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A mother who quietly agrees, yet refuses to settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home never settles, which describes a roaming herder or traveller.

clue.text: Keeping on temporary accommodation (and keeping old home)

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

indicators.note: keeping here means holding, so the home word holds the old letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone staying on in a temporary place while hanging on to the old house.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reuses 'keeping' as the containment signal for the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding on to something, rather than letting it go, is the act of keeping it.

clue.text: Do angels have to do it after start of show? It's a bit naughty

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the word show

parts.words: Do angels have to do it
parts.note: angels are pictured playing harps, so they would need harp practice

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether angels rehearse before a show, followed by a wink about naughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The angels' imagined task is HARP PRACTICE, placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand but not quite criminal dealing is mildly dishonest behaviour, a bit naughty rather than outright crooked.
